region: Industry City, Sunset Park · Brooklyn, New York
about: This is the whiskey Fort Hamilton was founded to make. Alex Clark, a British bartender who came up in New York’s cocktail revival, and his wife, Amy Grindeland, started the distillery in 2016 to recreate New York rye, the style made across the Northeast before bourbon took over. The label shows the Hearts of Oak militia’s August 1775 raid on lower Manhattan, an episode tied to Alexander Hamilton, for whom Brooklyn’s Fort Hamilton is named.

The mash bill follows pre-Revolutionary practice: 90% rye and 10% malted barley, with no corn, all grown at Migliorelli Farm in Tivoli in the Hudson Valley. It is distilled at Taconic Distillery in Stanfordville on a 12-foot Vendome column still and made under New York’s Empire Rye designation. Each barrel is a 30-gallon, number 3 char American oak cask, bottled one barrel at a time at 90 proof with no chill filtration, coloring or flavoring.

The distillery describes bright caramel, juniper berry, spearmint and lemon zest over a frame of caramelized sugar, cherry, white pepper and tree bark. Because each bottle comes from one barrel, the age and character shift slightly from release to release. Leaving out corn keeps the rye’s spice and herbal edge at the front, much as the whiskey would have tasted in a colonial New York tavern.
